theory.intro: The **best buy** is the offer that gives the best value for money. Offers come in different sized packages, so the total price cannot be compared directly. Instead compare the price of **one unit** — one item, one gram, one litre — and choose the lowest.
facts: A **unit price** is the cost of one unit, e.g. $\$0.42$ per egg or $\$7.40$ per kg.
The **lowest price per unit** is the best buy.
Compared the other way round — the amount you get for $\$1$ — the **highest** quantity per dollar is the best buy.
Two offers can only be compared once both are written in the **same units**, e.g. write $0.5$ kg as $500$ g.
The cheapest package is **not** always the best buy: a small pack can cost less in total but more per unit.
steps: Convert the amounts to the same units
Divide to find the unit price of each option
Choose the lowest price per unit

foundation.question_text: Which is the best buy: $6$ eggs for $\$2.55$, or $8$ eggs for $\$3.50$?
foundation.solution_text:
Option 1: $\dfrac{\$2.55}{6\text{ eggs}} = \dfrac{\$0.425}{1\text{ egg}}$
Option 2: $\dfrac{\$3.50}{8\text{ eggs}} = \dfrac{\$0.4375}{1\text{ egg}}$
$\$0.425 < \$0.4375$, so $6$ eggs for $\$2.55$ is the best buy.

foundation.question_text: A bakery sells donuts in three packages: $4$ for $\$1.55$, $6$ for $\$2.30$ and $10$ for $\$3.75$. Determine the best buy. Do not round your answers.
foundation.solution_text:
Option 1: $\dfrac{\$1.55}{4\text{ donuts}} = \dfrac{\$0.3875}{1\text{ donut}}$
Option 2: $\dfrac{\$2.30}{6\text{ donuts}} = \dfrac{\$0.3833\ldots}{1\text{ donut}}$
Option 3: $\dfrac{\$3.75}{10\text{ donuts}} = \dfrac{\$0.375}{1\text{ donut}}$
$\$0.375$ is the lowest, so $10$ donuts for $\$3.75$ is the best buy.

foundation.question_text: Coffee is sold in a $200$ g jar for $\$1.55$ and in a $0.5$ kg jar for $\$3.70$. Which is the best buy?
foundation.solution_text:
$0.5$ kg $= 500$ g
Option 1: $\dfrac{\$1.55}{200\text{ g}} = \dfrac{\$7.75}{1000\text{ g}}$
Option 2: $\dfrac{\$3.70}{500\text{ g}} = \dfrac{\$7.40}{1000\text{ g}}$
$\$7.40 < \$7.75$, so the $0.5$ kg jar is the best buy.

foundation.question_text: Potatoes are sold in $2$ kg bags for $\$3.50$ and in $7$ kg bags for $\$12.50$. By working out how many kilograms you get for $\$1$, determine the best buy. Answer to two decimal places.
foundation.solution_text:
Option 1: $\dfrac{2\text{ kg}}{\$3.50} = \dfrac{0.57\text{ kg}}{\$1}$
Option 2: $\dfrac{7\text{ kg}}{\$12.50} = \dfrac{0.56\text{ kg}}{\$1}$
More kilograms per dollar is better value, so the $2$ kg bag is the best buy.

foundation.question_text: Pencils are sold in packs of $4$ for $\$3.00$ and packs of $6$ for $\$4.35$. Find the cost of $12$ pencils from each option and state the best buy.
foundation.solution_text:
Option 1: $12 \div 4 = 3$ packs
$3 \times \$3.00 = \$9.00$
Option 2: $12 \div 6 = 2$ packs
$2 \times \$4.35 = \$8.70$
For the same $12$ pencils the $6$-packs cost less, so the $6$-pack is the best buy.

foundation.question_text: Juice is sold as $400$ mL for $\$2.20$, $1$ L for $\$4.80$ and $1.5$ L for $\$7.50$. Which bottle costs the least, and which bottle is the best buy?
foundation.solution_text:
Option 1: $\dfrac{\$2.20}{0.4\text{ L}} = \dfrac{\$5.50}{1\text{ L}}$
Option 2: $\dfrac{\$4.80}{1\text{ L}}$
Option 3: $\dfrac{\$7.50}{1.5\text{ L}} = \dfrac{\$5.00}{1\text{ L}}$
The $400$ mL bottle costs the least at $\$2.20$, but it has the highest price per litre.
$\$4.80$ is the lowest price per litre, so the $1$ L bottle is the best buy.

development.question_text: At a wholesaler, onions cost $\$8.50$ for an $8$ kg bag. In the supermarket a $2$ kg bag costs $\$2.10$. In which shop are the onions better value?
development.solution_text:
Wholesaler: $\dfrac{\$8.50}{8\text{ kg}} = \dfrac{\$1.0625}{1\text{ kg}}$
Supermarket: $\dfrac{\$2.10}{2\text{ kg}} = \dfrac{\$1.05}{1\text{ kg}}$
$\$1.05 < \$1.0625$, so the onions are better value at the supermarket, even though the bag is smaller.

development.question_text: Sugar is sold in four different sized packets: $100$ g for $\$0.40$, $500$ g for $\$1.65$, $1$ kg for $\$3.50$ and $2$ kg for $\$6.90$. Which is the best buy?
development.solution_text:
$100$ g: $\dfrac{\$0.40}{0.1\text{ kg}} = \dfrac{\$4.00}{1\text{ kg}}$
$500$ g: $\dfrac{\$1.65}{0.5\text{ kg}} = \dfrac{\$3.30}{1\text{ kg}}$
$1$ kg: $\dfrac{\$3.50}{1\text{ kg}}$
$2$ kg: $\dfrac{\$6.90}{2\text{ kg}} = \dfrac{\$3.45}{1\text{ kg}}$
$\$3.30$ is the lowest, so $500$ g for $\$1.65$ is the best buy.

development.question_text: Cordial is sold as a $1$ L bottle for $\$3.85$, or as a pack of $12 \times 300$ mL bottles for $\$11.40$. Which is better value?
development.solution_text:
Pack volume: $12 \times 300\text{ mL} = 3600\text{ mL} = 3.6$ L
Option 1: $\dfrac{\$3.85}{1\text{ L}}$
Option 2: $\dfrac{\$11.40}{3.6\text{ L}} = \dfrac{\$3.17}{1\text{ L}}$
$\$3.17 < \$3.85$, so the $12$-pack is better value.

development.question_text: Chips are sold in a $45$ g bag for $\$2.10$ and a $150$ g bag for $\$6.50$. Find how many grams you get for $\$1$ from each bag, to one decimal place, and state the best buy.
development.solution_text:
Option 1: $\dfrac{45\text{ g}}{\$2.10} = \dfrac{21.4\text{ g}}{\$1}$
Option 2: $\dfrac{150\text{ g}}{\$6.50} = \dfrac{23.1\text{ g}}{\$1}$
The higher number of grams per dollar is the better value, so the $150$ g bag is the best buy.

development.question_text: Rice is sold in $3$ kg bags for $\$7.20$ and in $5$ kg bags for $\$11.75$. Find the cost of $15$ kg of rice from each option and state the best buy.
development.solution_text:
Option 1: $15 \div 3 = 5$ bags
$5 \times \$7.20 = \$36.00$
Option 2: $15 \div 5 = 3$ bags
$3 \times \$11.75 = \$35.25$
For the same $15$ kg the $5$ kg bags cost less, so the $5$ kg bag is the best buy.

development.question_text: Sunscreen comes in four sizes: $500$ mL for $\$4.75$, $600$ mL for $\$5.40$, $750$ mL for $\$7.40$ and $1200$ mL for $\$10.90$. Marcus says the biggest bottle must be the best buy. Is he correct?
development.solution_text:
$500$ mL: $\dfrac{\$4.75}{500\text{ mL}} = \dfrac{\$0.950}{100\text{ mL}}$
$600$ mL: $\dfrac{\$5.40}{600\text{ mL}} = \dfrac{\$0.900}{100\text{ mL}}$
$750$ mL: $\dfrac{\$7.40}{750\text{ mL}} = \dfrac{\$0.987}{100\text{ mL}}$
$1200$ mL: $\dfrac{\$10.90}{1200\text{ mL}} = \dfrac{\$0.908}{100\text{ mL}}$
Marcus is incorrect. The $600$ mL bottle has the lowest price per $100$ mL, so it is the best buy; the $1200$ mL bottle is only second best.

mastery.question_text: Shop A sells $500$ g boxes of cereal for $\$4.20$ with a "buy $3$, get $1$ free" offer. Shop B sells a $2$ kg box for $\$12.90$. Which shop offers the better value?
mastery.solution_text:
Shop A, taking the offer: $4$ boxes $= 4 \times 500\text{ g} = 2000\text{ g} = 2$ kg
Cost of $4$ boxes: $3 \times \$4.20 = \$12.60$
$\dfrac{\$12.60}{2\text{ kg}} = \dfrac{\$6.30}{1\text{ kg}}$
Shop B: $\dfrac{\$12.90}{2\text{ kg}} = \dfrac{\$6.45}{1\text{ kg}}$
$\$6.30 < \$6.45$, so Shop A offers the better value.

mastery.question_text: A $750$ g pack of pasta costs $\$6.30$. A $1.2$ kg pack is about to go on sale. What is the highest price the $1.2$ kg pack could be and still be the better buy?
mastery.solution_text:
$\dfrac{\$6.30}{750\text{ g}} = \dfrac{\$8.40}{1000\text{ g}}$
At the same unit price, $1.2$ kg would cost $1.2 \times \$8.40 = \$10.08$
To be the better buy the $1.2$ kg pack must have a lower price per kilogram, so it must be priced below $\$10.08$.

mastery.question_text: Mario must decide which is better value: $200$ g of pasta for $80$ c, or $500$ g of pasta for $\$1.95$. He calculates $200 \div 80 = 2.5$ and $500 \div 195 = 2.56$, then chooses the $200$ g pack because $2.5$ is smaller. Explain why he is incorrect and state the best buy.
mastery.solution_text:
Mario divided quantity by cost, so his numbers are grams per cent, not cents per gram.
Option 1: $\dfrac{200\text{ g}}{80\text{ c}} = \dfrac{2.5\text{ g}}{1\text{ c}}$
Option 2: $\dfrac{500\text{ g}}{195\text{ c}} = \dfrac{2.56\text{ g}}{1\text{ c}}$
With quantity per dollar the **highest** value is the best buy, not the lowest, so Mario chose the wrong pack.
The $500$ g pack for $\$1.95$ is the best buy.
